title: Ordered sets: comparison, bounds, and quotients

based_on.title: Mathematical foundations: (3) Lattice theory — Part I

summary: Compare elements in partial orders, distinguish extrema from bounds, and turn a preorder into an ordered set of classes.
abstract: Comparing sets by inclusion or positive integers by divisibility leads to a partial order, where some pairs need not be comparable. This makes “smallest” subtler than it is for numbers: an element can have nothing smaller without being below every other element. Every nonempty finite ordered set has elements with nothing smaller and elements with nothing larger, even when it has no single smallest or largest element. Bounds extend these comparisons to elements outside a chosen set; when a smallest upper bound or largest lower bound exists, it is unique.
